conventions.convention: An observer n at p satisfies g(n,n)=−1 and g(n,N)<0, with Lorentzian signature (−,+,+,+). Zero is excluded from causal vectors.

A type (r,s) tensor evaluates r covector arguments followed by s vector arguments. Coordinate indices range over 0,1,2,3; Einstein summation contracts one upper and one lower occurrence. Fields are C∞.
The canonical tensor-bundle construction assumes Countable Choice, uses supplied countable coordinate covers, and includes the empty manifold and r=s=0.

Congruences are smooth observer fields on nonempty open sets. Adapted spatial coordinates are constant on each connected interval of an observer curve inside the chart; labels need not agree after exit and re-entry. An adapted coordinate field need not equal n.

A tetrad has Gram matrix diag(−1,1,1,1); future direction constrains its zeroth member, without imposing a spatial orientation. For F_A=Σ_B Λ^B_A E_B, upper tensor slots transform with Λ inverse and lower slots with Λ.

c is a positive mathematical parameter. E_n(P)=−c g(P,n), q_n(P)=h_n(P), and m(P)=sqrt(−g(P,P))/c only for g(P,P)≤0. U=P/m has squared norm −c², whereas u=U/c has squared norm −1. These mathematical items assert no measurement or physical unit identification.

load_bearing.statement: h_n(v)=v+g(n,v)n is a linear idempotent with kernel Rn and image n⊥. Every v has the unique orthogonal decomposition v=−g(v,n)n+h_n(v). The projection identity is g(h_n(v),h_n(w))=g(v,w)+g(v,n)g(n,w), and n⊥ is three-dimensional positive definite.

For an observer n, γ(w)=−g(n,w)>0 for nonzero future causal w. For future unit timelike w, γ(w)≥1, with equality exactly when w=n, and g(h_n(w),h_n(w))=γ(w)²−1. For unit timelike w, future direction is equivalent to g(n,w)<0 and past direction to g(n,w)>0.

Assume Countable Choice. On a smooth boundaryless four-manifold, coordinate evaluation bijections define a unique smooth vector-bundle structure on the disjoint union of type (r,s) tensor fibres. Transitions apply J_yx to upper indices and its inverse to lower indices, satisfy the cocycle identities, and give the smooth-section criterion in one atlas equivalently every smooth chart.

For future unit timelike u, γ=−g(n,u)≥1 and w=c h_n(u)/γ satisfy u=γ(n+w/c), w∈n⊥ and g(w,w)=c²(1−γ⁻²)<c². This decomposition is unique, and the converse gives a bijection with pairs (λ,v) satisfying λ≥1, v∈n⊥ and g(v,v)=c²(1−λ⁻²).
E²=c²(g(q,q)−g(P,P)) for every P. Nonzero future causal P has E>0. Future timelike P has E=mc²γ, q=mγw and E²=m²c⁴+c²g(q,q); future null P has E=c sqrt(g(q,q))>0.

For an observer congruence, α=n♭ is a nowhere-zero smooth one-form and ker α is a smooth rank-three distribution. It is integrable if and only if α∧dα=0. When this holds, local coordinates make the rest spaces tangent to the level hypersurfaces of u⁰.
For every observer congruence n on a nonempty open U and every p∈U, there is a chart on U′⊆U containing p with n=∂/∂u⁰; its spatial coordinates are constant along integral curves contained in U′.

concerns.concern: Verification 2.1 says 'g(u,n)=−g(n,u)=−γ'. The metric is symmetric and the supplied preceding example establishes g(n,u)=−γ, so −g(n,u)=+γ. The displayed chain is false as written. The intended equality g(u,n)=g(n,u)=−γ gives the stated energy, and the surrounding independent computations support that intended result.

The Observer-relative quantities bullet says 'Observer energy, spatial momentum and rest mass are defined with respect to a chosen observer'. The cited definition gives m(P)=sqrt(−g(P,P))/c, independently of n. The wording should distinguish invariant rest mass from observer-dependent energy and spatial momentum.

alerts.finding: The deflection readout calls q_i=h_{n_i}(W(s_i)) 'the spatial projection of clause (b) of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]'. Clause (b) defines the rest space; clause (c) defines h_n. The formula and positivity use are correct, but the exact supplier locator is wrong.

Proof 3.1 says the derivations 'agree on a basis of germs and hence are equal'. Coordinate germs are not a vector-space basis of the algebra of smooth germs. Steps 1.1–2.1 correctly use them as a separating family for derivations, justified by their unique coordinate representation; the final wording should retain that distinction.

seams_checked.note: The manifold, signature, smooth metric, inverse metric and future-direction definitions agree with the framework suppliers; Countable Choice and the mathematical-only reading are retained.
Flat metric and N=∂₀ specialize the supplied Lorentzian geometry and future-direction conventions correctly.
Tensor sections and contraction are used at their smooth scope. Reverse Cauchy–Schwarz is explicitly obtained by positive normalization from the unit-timelike pairing result.
Tensor components, metric slot movement, positive normal fibres and normalized pairing inequalities preserve the supplier hypotheses.
Constant components in the global identity chart define smooth tensors through the one-atlas criterion; algebraic tidal counterexamples retain the observer distinction.
Smooth component constructions and contractions are compatible. Observer-adapted pointwise orthonormal bases are constructed using the positive rest space and Gram–Schmidt.
The projector δ+n⊗n♭, observer-current split, congruence curves and positive normalization of a future timelike Killing field agree with the suppliers.
Flat observer fields are explicitly smooth, future-directed and unit timelike; energy-density observer dependence is kept distinct from conservation and positivity.
The inertial coordinate frame is a tetrad. Velocity and energy expansions use future timelike P with m>0 and the supplied c-normalizations.
The numerical velocity example restates the projection identity and mass-shell data with the correct unit-vector normalization.
Tetrad curvature evaluations use covariant-slot factors. The static congruence is future unit timelike, and redshift positivity uses nonzero future null tangents.
Static observer curves and clock-ratio examples preserve the congruence definition; clock interpretation comes from separate suppliers.
n=c⁻¹∂t is unit normalized; the congruence designation explicitly excludes the empty product. The observer-energy formula and future-null positivity are preserved.
The redshift example uses E_n(V)=−c g(V,n)=c²Vᵗ and preserves future-null and affine-parameter conditions.
The screen is obtained inside the positive three-dimensional rest space by removing a unit spatial direction; tensor and projector uses agree with the suppliers.
The rank-three spatial projector is diag(0,1,1,1) in an observer-adapted tetrad; the half-trace counterexample uses that rank correctly.
Temporal-function positivity and hypersurface-normal arguments use observer pairing after positive normalization. Geodesic congruences add ∇_n n=0 explicitly.
The radial focusing example explicitly requires a smooth future unit timelike field on an open set before calling it a congruence.

Observer definitions, energy positivity and spatial projection content are mathematically faithful, but the deflection readout incorrectly locates the spatial projection in clause (b), rather than clause (c); routed in alerts.
The example uses the unit observer U/c and computes E=−c g(W,U/c)=−g(W,U). Illustrative records remain separate from empirical observations.
Adapted charts use the normalized observer field. Reverse inequalities and null-pairing rigidity are derived explicitly from the positive rest-space split, Cauchy–Schwarz and strict observer pairing.

Tensor operations retain their variance conventions. The dust reduction explicitly declares γ=−g and changes its orthonormal normalization to (+,−,−,−); its comoving-parallel gauge is additional supplied data.
